subject: FullStack: additional project keys, proration and renewal coordination
messages:
From: Aaron Brooks <aaron.brooks@fullstack.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@fullstack.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: keys for two new projects + proration on renewal

Hi Mina,

Quick one — we want to bring two new projects (checkout-widget, mobile-sync) onto Redwood before our June 30 renewal. Can you confirm:

- How many additional API keys we should request per project (they use multiple environments: dev/stage/prod)
- Whether we can prorate the committed capacity for the remainder of the term (we're mid-cycle)
- Any impact to our per-token rates if we add the projects now

Attaching a short spreadsheet with estimated call volumes. If possible we'd like to stagger activation next week.

Thanks,
Aaron
Head of Platform, FullStack Inc
attachments: credential_matrix.csv

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Aaron Brooks <aaron.brooks@fullstack.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-28T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: keys for two new projects + proration on renewal

Aaron — thanks for the details and the volume spreadsheet. Short answers up front:

- Recommend 3 keys per project (dev/stage/prod) + 1 rotating integration key for CI, so 4 per project total.
- We can prorate the committed capacity for new projects for the remainder of the billing cycle; I'll get numbers.
- Adding projects shouldn't change your unit rates unless you cross the next capacity tier — I'll confirm thresholds.

Action plan:
1) I'll pull proration numbers and a pricing delta (Ben).
2) Marissa will draft a minimal SOW amendment for the two projects and the key matrix.
3) If FullStack signs the amendment, we will schedule staged key issuance (dev first) next Thu/Fri.

Putting Marissa and Ben on thread to pick up the details.

Best,
Mina
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | mina@redwood.com

On Thu, May 28, 2026 at 09:12 Aaron Brooks <aaron.brooks@fullstack.com> wrote:
> Hi Mina,
> 
> Quick one — we want to bring two new projects (checkout-widget, mobile-sync) onto Redwood before our June 30 renewal...

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-28T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Proration numbers + tier impact for FullStack

Folks — I ran the numbers based on Aaron's estimates. Key points:

- If FullStack takes on the two projects now (estimated +1.2B tokens/month peak), prorated additional commit for the remaining 33 days of the term is ~ $18,600.
- If they wait until next billing period, starting commit is the full month; upfront cost is slightly higher but cleaner accounting.
- Current committed tier would need to increase to the next bucket if peak traffic forecasts are accurate; unit rate drops slightly in the higher commit but total spend increases.

Attached pricing-proration-breakdown.xlsx with line items.

Recommendation: offer a prorated addendum now and include a 30-day usage review to adjust the commit if traffic is lower than forecast. That reduces upfront friction.

Ben
Director, Account Strategy
attachments: pricing-proration-breakdown.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Aaron Brooks <aaron.brooks@fullstack.com>, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-29T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Draft SOW amendment and credential matrix

Aaron — attaching a draft SOW amendment and the credential matrix layout for the two projects. Highlights:

- Amendment will add the two projects to the scope, include prorated commit of $18,600 for 33 days, then roll into standard monthly billing on July 1.
- We propose 4 keys per project as Mina suggested. The credential_matrix.csv shows suggested naming + environment tags.
- We'll include a 30-day usage review clause with an option to adjust the commit or provide temporary overage credits.

Please review and flag any internal approvals needed on your side. Priyom, can you confirm the SOW language on the review clause?

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise AM
attachments: SOW-FullStack-v2.pdf, credential_matrix.csv

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW amendment and credential matrix

Marissa — language looks fine. Suggest we add a short paragraph that outlines rollback/fallback behavior: if commit adjustment is requested within the 30-day review and usage exceeds original forecast, we keep overage billing at the current rate and schedule a mid-cycle adjustment for capacity. Keeps both sides protected.

Also recommend we add explicit owner/responsibility table for activation dates (FullStack ops to confirm dev key schedule, Redwood to issue keys and rotate CI key).

I'll add those lines and resend.

Priyom
Senior AM Operations

Thanks team — reviewed the SOW and the matrix. A few quick notes from our side:

- Confirmed: we will need 4 keys per project.
- Ops requests activation for checkout-widget (dev) on Tue Jun 8 and mobile-sync (dev) on Thu Jun 10.
- We accept the prorated charge and the 30-day review clause but would like a 10% pre-approved credit if usage exceeds forecast during the first 14 days to avoid immediate overages while we tune.

Can Marissa/Ben confirm if the 10% temporary credit is doable? If so we can sign the amendment today and get DocuSign out.

Aaron
Head of Platform, FullStack Inc
